history.quote: Freeboard. The additional height that adds a factor of safety above the base-flood elevation (or flood level) for purposes of floodplain management. ... The freeboard requirement for the City of Tampa is six (6) inches.) ... 5-111.6.2.1. Residential construction. New construction or substantial improvement of any residential structure shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevation no lower than the design flood elevation. [Design flood elevation. See Freeboard.] (Ord. No. 2009-27, § 3, 2-19-09)

other_height_rules: Current: no local lowest-floor freeboard; elevations come from the Florida Building Code (FBC-R R322 / FBC-B 1612, which itself requires BFE+1 ft for residential) plus local design-flood definitions. AO zones: design flood elevation = highest existing grade at building perimeter + FIRM depth number (3 ft if no depth number). Accessory structures: flood-resistant materials and utilities to BFE+1 ft. 2002-2021 code: unnumbered A zones lowest floor at least 2 ft above highest adjacent grade (Ord. 2002-66 / 2004-64).
quote: Sec. 5-121.244 Technical amendments to the Florida Building Code, Building ... Amend Chapter 16, Section 1612 Flood Loads, as follows: 1612.4.1 Reserved. 1612.4.3. Modification of ASCE 24 Chapter 4 ... (Ord. No. 2024-15, § 2(Exh. A), 2-1-2024). [Sec. 5-121.246 amends FBC-R R322 only for enclosures (R322.2.2, R322.3.5, R322.3.6); no lowest-floor freeboard; the word 'freeboard' does not appear in Sec. 5-121 (Supplement 148, 2025-12-18).]
date_quote: Supplement 140 (2023-10-05), Sec. 5-111 Floodplain Management, every section: "(Ord. No. 2021-8, § 2(Exh. A), 2-4-2021)"; no 'freeboard' / six-inch text anywhere in Art. II definitions or Art. III. Earlier Sec. 5-111 'Flood Resistant Construction' (Supp. 128, 2020-11 and Supp. 132) still contained 'The freeboard requirement for the City of Tampa is six (6) inches.'
notes: Measured from Municode CodeBank versions via api.municode.com (product 10132). Supps 52 (2004-12), 62 (2007-09), 66 (2008-12): Sec. 5-111 'Residential construction ... elevation no lower than the base flood elevation' (Ord. 2002-66, 2-28-02; 2005-279) -> 0 ft local freeboard before 2009. Supp 69 (2009-09) first shows 'Design flood elevation. See Freeboard' and 'The freeboard requirement for the City of Tampa is six (6) inches' with Ord. No. 2009-27 (2-19-09); same in Supps 86 (2014), 119 (2018), 132. Ord. No. 2021-8 (2-4-2021) replaced Sec. 5-111 with the Florida model floodplain ordinance (FBC-based) and dropped the 6-inch local freeboard; re-codified as Sec. 5-121 by Ord. 2024-15 (2-1-2024), still no local freeboard. So the binding minimum for new houses since 2021 is the FBC (BFE+1 ft in FBC-R since its 2017/6th-edition era; see state_codes). 0.0 here means no LOCAL freeboard beyond the state code, not floor-at-BFE. Exact 2009 effective date taken as adoption date; Supp 132 (published 2021-08-05 but with lower job id than Supp 133) still showed the old text, which is a codification lag, not evidence the 6 inches lasted past 2021.

history.quote: Sec. 18-122. - Florida Building Code, local technical amendments, flood damage prevention standards. ... 1612.4.1 Elevation requirements. The minimum elevation requirements shall be as specified in ASCE 24 or the base flood elevation plus 1 foot, whichever is higher. ... R322.2.1 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures in flood hazard areas not designated as Coastal A Zones shall have the lowest floors elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher. ... (Ord. No. 14-20, § 6, 8-19-14)

other_height_rules: LDC 902.2 (stormwater): finished floor at least 16 inches above the highest street crown between the side-building lines (unless approved otherwise) and never below the 100-yr floodplain; in open/closed drainage basins the minimum habitable finished floor must be above the highest of the flood-damage-prevention elevation, recorded County-observed high water + 1 ft, and modeled 100-yr (24-h or 10-day) ponding + 1 ft. LDC 1104.6: critical facilities BFE+2 ft or 500-yr elevation; accessory structures materials/utilities to BFE+1 ft.
quote: Current Sec. 18-122 (Supp. 94, 2026) amends FBC 107.3.5, 202 (substantial improvement 49 percent), 1612.4.4 enclosure limitations, R322.2.2, R322.3.5, R322.3.6 only; it contains no R322.2.1 or 1612.4.1 elevation amendment and no 'plus 1 foot' text. LDC 1104.6 'Flood Hazard Reduction' defers building elevation to 'the Florida Building Code, as amended by Pasco County'. (Ord. No. 14-20, § 6, 8-19-14; Ord. No. 22-43, § 1, 8-24-22; Ord. No. 26-23, § 3, ...)
date_quote: Supp. 84 Update 1 (2022-08-24): Sec. 18-122 history '(Ord. No. 14-20, § 6, 8-19-14; Ord. No. 22-43, § 1, 8-24-22)', no R322.2.1 / 'plus 1 foot' text; Supp. 82 Update 1 (2022-02-22) and all earlier versions back to Supp. 63 Update 2 (2014-11-05) carried the R322.2.1 'base flood elevation plus 1 foot' amendment with history '(Ord. No. 14-20, § 6, 8-19-14)'.
notes: Measured from Municode CodeBank (product 10281 Code of Ordinances; 14292 LDC). Local BFE+1 ft (A, Coastal A and V zones, via FBC local technical amendments Sec. 18-122) is documented from Ord. No. 14-20 (8-19-2014) until Ord. No. 22-43 (8-24-2022) deleted it; by then the FBC itself (6th ed. 2017 onward) requires BFE+1 ft for residential, so the effective requirement did not drop - only the local duplicate went away. 0.0 = no local freeboard beyond the state code. Before 2014: Code Sec. 18-144 (Ord. 07-20, 2007) incorporated flood rules from LDC chapter 701 (later Sec. 1104), whose pre-2020 text is not on Municode (LDC versions start 2020). An unsigned draft ordinance (http://www.ordinancewatch.com/files/72011/LocalGovernment68468.pdf, effective-date clause 'March 15, 2012') proposed the same BFE+1 ft amendments to the 2010 FBC 'TO RETAIN EXISTING FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTION STANDARDS', implying the LDC already required BFE+1 ft before 2012, but Municode versions of 2012-2013 show no Sec. 18-122, so its adoption is unconfirmed and the start year of local freeboard is unknown (first_freeboard_year null, history_complete false). The 2014 history entry year is the documented-in-force year, not proven start. Pasco 2009/2024 LMS PDFs contained no freeboard adoption date.

other_height_rules: Appendix E local technical amendment (Ord. 18-37, 10-23-2018; Res. 21-113, 10-12-2021) applies FBC-R R322.3.2 V-zone elevation (bottom of lowest horizontal member at BFE+1 ft if parallel to wave approach, BFE+2 ft if perpendicular, or DFE) to Coastal A Zones as well; the +1/+2 ft text itself is the FBC's. Accessory structures: flood-resistant materials and utilities to BFE+1 ft. AO zones: DFE = highest existing grade + depth number. Pre-2015 Ch. 170: AO lowest floor at depth number above highest adjacent grade, or at least 2 ft if none specified (Ord. 83-9).
quote: APPENDIX E - LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE AND TECHNICAL AMENDMENTS TO THE FLORIDA BUILDING CODE ... R322.3.2 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures erected within coastal high hazard areas and Coastal A Zones, shall be elevated so that the bottom of the lowest horizontal structural members supporting the lowest floor ... is: 1.1 Located at or above the base flood elevation plus 1 foot or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher, if ... parallel ... 1.2 Located at the base flood elevation plus 2 feet, or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher, if ... perpendicular ... (Ord. No. 18-37, § 4, 10-23-18; Res. No. 21-113, § 1.I, 10-12-21). [No R322.2.1 (A-zone) amendment; Ch. 158 Floodplain Management contains no lowest-floor freeboard; 'freeboard' appears only as a definition in Sec. 158-182.]
date_quote: Supplement 75 (2012-02-21), Sec. 170-157 Specific standards: "(1) Residential construction. New construction or substantial improvement of any residential structure shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated to or above base flood elevation." (Ch. 170 Art. III Flood Damage Prevention derived from Ord. No. 77-12, 5-31-77, amended 83-9, 87-34, 90-15 ...)
notes: Measured from Municode CodeBank (product 10274). 2012 and 2014 (Supp. 85) versions: Ch. 170 Flood Damage Prevention requires residential lowest floor at or above BFE (no freeboard), V zone lowest supporting member at BFE. Ord. 15-21 (5-19-2015) replaced it with Ch. 158 Floodplain Management (Florida model, defers elevations to the FBC); Supp. 89 (2015) and Supp. 95 (2017) contain no 'plus 1 foot' text. Appendix E (from Ord. 18-37, 2018) amends only R322.3.2 (V/Coastal A) with the FBC's own +1/+2 ft wording, plus enclosure limits. So no LOCAL A-zone freeboard has been found in any version 2012-2026; new houses get the state FBC requirement (BFE+1 ft in FBC-R since the 2017/6th ed.; see state_codes). history_complete=true means no local freeboard was ever found, not a start date. Not checked: pre-2012 versions (Municode CodeBank starts 2012), and the separate Pinellas stormwater manual, which may set finished-floor rules relative to modeled flood stages.

other_height_rules: Where no BFE has been established the RFPE is 'at least 0 feet above the highest adjacent grade' (per the Village's 2024 handout quoting the ordinance). RFPE (BFE+1) applies to the reference level: top of lowest floor or bottom of lowest attendant utility/ductwork in A zones; bottom of lowest horizontal structural member or lowest utility in VE zones (2010 code definition of reference level).
quote: Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation means the "base flood elevation" plus the "freeboard". In "special flood hazard areas" where base flood elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus 1 foot of freeboard. In "special flood hazard areas" where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least 0 feet above the highest adjacent grade. ... The Village of Bald Head Island has adopted a 1-foot freeboard.
date_quote: Village Council Regular Session, Friday, December 13, 2019, AGENDA: "4. PUBLIC HEARING-FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTION ORDINANCE "FREEBOARD" 5. OLD BUSINESS 5.1 Adoption of the Free Board Definition Text Amendment of the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance [attachments: Requested_amendment_to_Regulatory_Flood_Protection_Elevation_Def.pdf; Village - ordinance amending the FDPO]". Preceded by Work Session Nov 15, 2019 (event_id=159): "6.1 Request to Amend Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance to require one (1') foot of freeboard."
notes: Before 2019 the local rule was 0 ft: the American Legal code PDF (Supplement No. 4, current through 2010-09-24; https://www.baldheadassociation.com/Images/bhinews/site/life/BHIVillageCodeOfOrdinances.pdf), Ch. 14 Art. II Flood Damage Prevention (Ord. of 9-26-2008): 'Regulatory flood protection elevation ... Where base flood elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus zero feet of freeboard.' A new FDPO was adopted at the 3-20-2018 council meeting (agenda event_id=127; text not retrievable), and the Nov 2019 request 'to require one (1') foot of freeboard' implies the 2018 FDPO still had 0 ft. 2019 = date of the public hearing/adoption agenda item; the adopted ordinance and the Dec 13 2019 minutes sit behind a Granicus login, so adoption on that date is inferred from the agenda (plus the 2024 Village handout confirming 1 ft is in force), not read from minutes. Scanned all ~250 Granicus agendas 2015-2026: no later freeboard change. American Legal current code (403) not read. NC state residential code freeboard is recorded separately.

other_height_rules: Where no BFE has been established, RFPE is at least 2 ft above highest adjacent grade. Reference level = top of lowest floor in Zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99; bottom of lowest horizontal structural member in VE. Mechanical/electrical equipment at or above RFPE; manufactured homes reference level at RFPE.
quote: "Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation" means the "Base Flood Elevation" plus the "Freeboard". In "Special Flood Hazard Areas" where Base Flood Elevations (BFEs) have been determined, this elevation shall be the BFE plus (2) feet freeboard). In "Special Flood Hazard Areas" where no BFE has been established, this elevation shall be at least two (2) feet above the highest adjacent grade. ... 7.1.5 B (1) Residential Construction. New construction and substantial improvement of any residential structure (including manufactured homes) shall have the reference level, including basement, elevated no lower than the Regulatory Flood Protection Elevation, as defined in Article 7.1.2 of this ordinance.
date_quote: Ordinance 2018-03 ... 7.1- FLOOD DAMAGE PREVENTION ORDINANCE (AUGUST 28, 2018) ... D. Effective Date. This ordinance shall become effective August 28, 2018. E. Adoption Certification. I hereby certify that this is a true and correct copy of the Flood Damage Prevention Ordinance as adopted by the Town Council of the Town of Saint James, North Carolina, on the 2nd day of July, 2018.
notes: The posted ordinance is a scanned PDF (no text layer); quotes were transcribed from page images (pp. 7, 19, 30) rendered with pdftoppm. 2 ft documented in force from Ord. 2018-03 (adopted 7-2-2018, effective 8-28-2018, with the 2018 Brunswick County FIRMs). That was a full re-adoption, so it is not proof freeboard began in 2018: the Town ordinance indexes (https://www.townofstjamesnc.org/media/ordinances/Ordinance_Index_1999-2015.pdf and Index_of_Ordinances_2016-Current.pdf) list 1999-5 'Flood Prevention Ordinance (December 7, 1999) (Revised and Amended May 2, 2006)', the 2007 UDO (07-004) and several UDO Article 7 amendments (11-004, 12-003, 12-005, ZTA 12-008, ZTA 13-002, 13-003, 2015-07), none of whose texts I could find online. Index also lists 2021-04 'Ordinance: Flood Damage Prevention Amendment 6/2/21', content not found; the Town site still posts the 2018 text as the FDPO, so I assume 2 ft is current but a 2021 change cannot be excluded. Hence current_since_year and first_freeboard_year are null. Town website meeting archive is JS-only and web.archive.org failed (connection reset).

other_height_rules: Shaded Zone X (0.2%-annual-chance area): residential lowest floor 24 in above the nearest adjacent A-zone BFE (Sec. 8.5-37). AO/AH: lowest floor at FIRM depth number + 24 in above highest adjacent grade, or at least 4 ft if no depth number (residential). V zones: bottom of lowest horizontal structural member at least 24 in above BFE (Sec. 8.5-36). Since Ord. O2023-834 (3-13-2023) the 24-in requirement explicitly covers ductwork and all utilities servicing the building.
quote: (1) Residential construction— New construction and substantial improvement of any residential structure shall have the lowest floor, (including basement, ductwork, and all utilities servicing the building) elevated to a minimum of twenty-four (24) inches above the base flood elevation. ... (Ord. No. 2000-511, Art. 5, § B, 5-8-2000; Ord. No. 2000-524, 9-11-2000; Ord. No. O2023-834, § 1, 3-13-23)
date_quote: Supplement 35 (2010-10-11), Sec. 8.5-32: "Residential construction— New construction and substantial improvement of any residential structure shall have the lowest floor, including basement, elevated a minimum of twenty-four (24) inches above the base flood elevation. ..." (Ord. No. 2000-511, Art. 5, § B, 5-8-2000; Ord. No. 2000-524, 9-11-2000)
notes: Measured from Municode CodeBank (product 11324; versions 2010-2025: Supps 35, 38, 39, 41, 42, 43 all have 24 in). The oldest online version (2010) attributes Sec. 8.5-32 only to Ord. 2000-511 (5-8-2000) and Ord. 2000-524 (9-11-2000), so the 24-inch rule dates from one of those 2000 ordinances (which one not determinable); whether an earlier (pre-2000) Nassau Bay ordinance already had freeboard is unknown, so current_since_year and first_freeboard_year are null and documented_in_force_by=2000. 2023 amendment (O2023-834) extended the rule to ductwork/utilities, not the height. City page https://www.nassaubay.com/730/Development-Requirements and FEMA case study (FY2022 elevation of 19 homes 'to at least two feet above the Base Flood Elevation per the city's freeboard requirements') confirm 2 ft current.
